Sumitra Bhati D/o Ram Kishor Ji Panwar, Aged About 35  Years, W/o Gyanchand Bhati, Bus Stand Ratkudiya Tehsil  Bhopalgarh District Jodhpur (Raj.)
2. Yajat Bhati S/o Gyanchand Bhati, Aged About 9 Years,

Through His Natural Guardian His Mother Smt. Sumitra  Bhati D/o Ramkishore Ji Panwar, W/o Gyanchand Bhati,
 Aged About 40 Years, R/o Bus Stand, Ratkudiya, Tehsil  Bhopalgarh, Distt. Jodhpur (Raj.)
 ----Petitioners  Versus Gyanchand Bhati S/o Ghenwar Ram Ji, Bavariyo Ka Bas Sangawas Village And Post Nimaj Thesil Jaitaran District Pali (Raj.)
 ----Respondent For Petitioner(s) : Mr. Manish on behalf of Mr.S.K.Maru For Respondent(s) : None present despite service  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE YOGENDRA KUMAR PUROHIT Order 05/05/2025 1.

The petitioners who are wife and son of respondent, have filed the present civil transfer application seeking transfer of Case No. 15/2024 "Gyanchand Bhati Vs. Yajat Bhati & Anr."
preferred by the respondent-husband under Section 6 of the Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act,
pending before Additional District Judge, Jaitaran, District Pali to the Family Court No.1, Jodhpur.

3. None present for the respondent despite service of notice.
No one was present on behalf of respondent on 27.3.2025 either.

4. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and perused the material available on record.
5.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the marriage between the petitioner-wife and respondent-husband was solemnized on 8.5.2004 at Village Ratkudiya, District Jodhpur as per Hindu rites and out of the said wedlock one son namely Yajat Bhati was born.

However, the petitioner-wife was treated cruelly and harassed for demand of dowry by the respondent- husband and his family members, therefore, she lodged an FIR with the Mahila Thana (Jodhpur Rural) for the offence under Section 498A, 406, 323 IPC.
She has also filed an application under Section 125 Cr.P.C. which is pending before Family Court No.1, Jodhpur.

However, with a view to harass and humiliate the petitioner, the respondent-husband has filed the aforesaid application under Section 6 of the Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act before ADJ, Jaitaran, District Pali.

6. Learned counsel for the petitioner further submitted that vide order dated 19.7.2024 passed by this Court in S.B.Civil Transfer Application No.83/2024 filed by the petitioner, the petition filed by the respondent-husband under Section 13 of the Hindu Marriage Act, before ADJ, Jaitaran has already been transferred to Family Court No.1, Jodhpur, which is pending consideration.
Learned counsel for the petitioner further submitted that the petitioner is a young lady and is presently residing with her parents at Village Ratkudiya, District Jodhpur along with her minor child.
It is very difficult and onerous for the petitioner to travel from her place of residence at Jodhpur to Jaitaran to attend and defend the case filed by her husband.
The aforesaid cases filed by the petitioner-wife are pending at Jodhpur.

The case filed by the respondent-husband under Section 13 of the Hindu Marriage Act at ADJ, Jaitaran, District Pali has already been transferred to Family Court No.1, Jodhpur vide order dated 19.07.2024 passed by this Court in S.B.Civil Transfer Application No.83/2024.

Thus, in the facts and circumstances of the case, in the interest of justice,
the case filed by the respondent-husband at Additional District Judge, Jaitaran, District Pali under Section 6 of the Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act deserves to be transferred to the Family Court No.1, Jodhpur.

entities.text: Additional District Judge, Jaitaran, District Pali
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 8. It is settled law that while considering transfer of case in matrimonial proceedings instituted by the husband, the convenience of the wife is to be looked into.

In this regard, recently, Hon'ble the Supreme Court in the matter of N.C.V. Aishwarya Vs. A.S.Saravana Karthik Sha, (Civil Appeal No.4894/2022 arising out of SLP (C) No.16465/2021) decided on 18.7.2022, while considering transfer of matrimonial case under Section 24 CPC, has observed as under:-
"The cardinal principle for exercise of power under Section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure is that the ends of justice should demand the transfer of the suit, appeal or other proceeding.

entities.text: N.C.V. Aishwarya Vs. A.S.Saravana Karthik Sha
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In matrimonial matters, wherever Courts are called upon to consider the plea of transfer, [2025:RJ-JD:21558] (4 of 4) [CTA-228/2024] the Sumitra Bhati vs Gyanchand Bhati (2025:Rj-Jd:21558) on 5 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129625160/
2

Courts have to take into consideration the economic soundness of both the parties,
the social strata of the spouses and their behavioural pattern, their standard of life prior to the marriage and subsequent thereto and the circumstances of both the parties in eking out their livelihood and under whose protective umbrella they are seeking their sustenance to life.
Given the prevailing socio-economic paradigm in the Indian society, generally, it is the wife's convenience which must be looked at while considering transfer."

9. Having considered the submissions made on behalf of the petitioner, looking to the facts and circumstances of the case noticed above and the settled position of law by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of N.C.V. Aishwarya (supra), the transfer application is allowed.
It is ordered that Case No.15/2024 pending before Additional District Judge, Jaitaran, District Pali be transferred to the Family Court No.1, Jodhpur.
The ADJ Jaitaran, District Pali is directed to send the record of the aforesaid case to the Family Court No.1, Jodhpur immediately.
The parties are directed to appear before the Family Court No.1, Jodhpur on 02.6.2025.
A copy of this order be sent to the Family Court No.1 Jodhpur and ADJ Jaitaran, District Pali forthwith.
Stay application also stands disposed of.

(YOGENDRA KUMAR PUROHIT),J 243-RP/-
